title: Ukraine Intercepts Russian Jet Drone Using Laser System
seoTitle: Ukraine downs Russian jet drone with laser defense system
dek: Ukrainian defense officials reported the first combat interception of a Russian jet-powered drone using a domestically produced laser defense system.
happened: On 25 November, Ukrainian presidential military adviser Serhii Beskrestnov stated that a Russian jet-powered strike drone was destroyed using a laser air defense system named Blisk or Blysk. The four-kilowatt directed-energy weapon was developed by Ukrainian defense firm Kamin Sky, also referred to as Carmine Sky, under a state-supported civilian air defense initiative. According to Asia Times, the laser system was deployed in early November to protect critical infrastructure around Kyiv at ranges of up to one kilometer. The system functions by concentrating heat on a fixed point to burn internal components mid-flight over several seconds. Beskrestnov noted that Ukraine's interception rate for newer Russian jet-powered Geran drones had dropped to approximately 57 percent compared to around 90 percent for older propeller-driven models, as Russia expanded monthly production of jet-powered models to as many as 3,000 units.

sides.says: Adviser Serhii Beskrestnov stated that the laser interception marks a major proof of concept, though he cautioned that serial production remains premature while trials against weather constraints and tracking limits continue.

Asia Times reported that directed-energy systems offer lower per-shot costs than conventional interceptor missiles, but face operational limits from atmospheric conditions like fog and potential countermeasures such as reflective coatings or evasive maneuvers.

next: Testing of the laser system will continue to evaluate performance across varying weather conditions and target speeds.
summary: Ukraine announced the first successful combat interception of a Russian jet-powered strike drone using a domestically developed laser air defense system. Presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov stated on 25 November that the system, named Blisk, downed a Russian drone deployed against critical infrastructure. Developed by Ukrainian defense firm Kamin Sky with state support, the laser provides a lower-cost alternative to traditional interceptor missiles. Officials emphasized that mass production is not yet planned as operational testing under adverse weather and combat conditions continues.
